name: Mary Lucy Cartwright
summary: British mathematician known for work on nonlinear differential equations and chaos theory.

name: J. E. Littlewood
summary: British mathematician and long-time collaborator of Mary Cartwright.

name: G. H. Hardy
summary: British mathematician who supervised Mary Cartwright's doctoral work.

name: E. C. Titchmarsh
summary: British mathematician who supervised Mary Cartwright when Hardy was away.

name: Girton College
summary: Women's constituent college of the University of Cambridge where Cartwright was a Fellow and Mistress.

name: St Hugh's College
summary: Women's constituent college of the University of Oxford where Cartwright studied.

name: University of Oxford
summary: University where Mary Cartwright completed her undergraduate and doctoral studies.

name: University of Cambridge
summary: University where Mary Cartwright worked as a lecturer and Mistress of Girton College.

name: Royal Society
summary: Learned society for science of which Cartwright was a Fellow and Council member.

name: London Mathematical Society
summary: Mathematical society of which Cartwright was the first woman president.

name: Radio Research Board
summary: British government board that requested mathematical guidance on radio engineering equations.

name: Aynho
summary: Village in Northamptonshire where Mary Cartwright was born and lived until 1926.

name: Midfield Lodge Nursing Home
summary: Nursing home where Mary Cartwright lived from 1994 until her death.

name: Addenbrooke's Hospital
summary: Hospital in Cambridge where Mary Cartwright was treated after a fall in 1994.

name: Van der Pol equation
summary: Nonlinear differential equation studied by Cartwright and Littlewood in relation to radio engineering.

name: Sylvester Medal
summary: Award given by the Royal Society which Cartwright received in 1964.

name: de Morgan Medal
summary: Highest honour of the London Mathematical Society awarded to Cartwright in 1968.

name: Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire
summary: British honour appointed to Cartwright in 1969.
